transcriber.keywords: Nabz, Hero, Honda, Bajaj, TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha, Royal Enfield, Splendor, Pulsar, Activa, Jupiter, Shine, Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, enquiry, enquiries, booking, bookings, stock, rolling stock, discount, offer, offers, scheme, finance, loan, EMI, reject, showroom, owner, sales manager, survey, normal, hold, Diwali
transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Marathi. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Marathi with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "खूप धन्यवाद, तुमचा दिवस छान जावो.", "काही हरकत नाही, त्रास दिल्याबद्दल माफ करा. तुमचा दिवस छान जावो.", "माफ करा, चुकीचा number लागला. तुमचा दिवस छान जावो.", "धन्यवाद, नमस्कार!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "ठीक आहे, [time] ला call करू. धन्यवाद.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Marathi to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Marathi, written in Devanagari. Never write Marathi words in Latin letters. Never switch to Hindi or any other language, even if the person does; if they speak English, understand it and keep replying in Marathi.
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz, AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, enquiries, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loan, reject, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, showroom, Google, public, listing, share, number, owner. Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Use simple, everyday spoken Marathi, the way people talk on the phone, not formal written Marathi.
- Be polite: use तुम्ही / आपण and their verb forms (सांगा, कराल). Don't say सर or मॅडम. You are female: use feminine forms for yourself (बोलतेय, करते, समजले).
- End every sentence with . or ? No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "नमस्कार, मी Nabz ची AI assistant बोलतेय. हे {dealer_name} आहे का? Owner किंवा sales manager शी बोलता येईल का?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "हो नक्की, मी line वर आहे."
G2 (first call): "नमस्कार, मी Nabz ची AI assistant बोलतेय. दर आठवड्याला {city} मधल्या {brand} dealers ना सहा छोटे प्रश्न विचारतो, फक्त दीड मिनिट लागेल. उत्तरं confidential राहतात, आणि call record होतोय. सुरू करूया का?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "दर आठवड्याला {city} मधल्या {brand} dealers ना सहा छोटे प्रश्न विचारतो, फक्त दीड मिनिट लागेल. उत्तरं confidential राहतात, आणि call record होतोय. सुरू करूया का?"
G3 (repeat call): "नमस्कार, Nabz ची AI assistant पुन्हा बोलतेय, मागच्या आठवड्यासाठी धन्यवाद. तेच सहा प्रश्न, दीड मिनिट. सुरू करूया का?"
Q1: "मागच्या आठवड्यापेक्षा या आठवड्यात enquiries जास्त आल्या, तेवढ्याच, की कमी?"
Q2: "आणि bookings, मागच्या आठवड्यापेक्षा जास्त, तेवढ्याच, की कमी?"
Q3: "या आठवड्यात साधारण किती bookings झाल्या?"
Q4: "आत्ताच्या विक्रीच्या हिशोबाने, आत्ताचा stock किती दिवस पुरेल?"
Q5: "{brand} वर discount आणि offers, मागच्या आठवड्यापेक्षा वाढतायत, तेवढेच आहेत, की कमी होतायत?"
Q6: "शेवटचा प्रश्न: मागच्या महिन्यापेक्षा, customers चे loan reject जास्त होतायत, तेवढेच, की कमी?"
P1 (they don't know): "अंदाजे सांगितलं तरी चालेल."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "जास्त, तेवढंच, की कमी?"
P3 (still no answer): "ठीक आहे, पुढे जाऊया."
X1 (close): "खूप धन्यवाद, तुमचा दिवस छान जावो."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "काही हरकत नाही. कधी call करू, आज नंतर की उद्या?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "ठीक आहे, [time] ला call करू. धन्यवाद."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "नाही, आम्ही काहीही विकत नाही. Nabz एक market research company आहे, जी संपूर्ण India मधली vehicle demand track करते."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "हो, मी AI assistant आहे. फक्त सहा प्रश्न, दीड मिनिट."
O3 (how did you get my number): "तुमच्या showroom च्या Google वरच्या public listing मधून."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "उत्तरं इतर dealers सोबत एकत्र मोजली जातात, तुमचं नाव कधीच share होत नाही. अंदाजे सांगितलं तरी चालेल."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "काही हरकत नाही, त्रास दिल्याबद्दल माफ करा. तुमचा दिवस छान जावो."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "माफ करा, चुकीचा number लागला. तुमचा दिवस छान जावो."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "तुम्ही owner किंवा sales manager आहात का?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "हो, सांगा." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "धन्यवाद, नमस्कार!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Marathi or English. The dealer's words may be written in Devanagari (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (माहीत नाही, कल्पना नाही, finance वाल्यांना माहीत). declined when they won't say (सांगणार नाही, सांगता येणार नाही, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example जास्त, वाढल्या, वाढतायत, जास्त आल्या, jaast).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example तेवढ्याच, तितकेच, सारखेच, same, बदल नाही, tevdhech). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said enquiries went down (for example कमी, कमी झाल्या, घटल्या, मंदी, kami). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "या आठवड्यात साधारण किती bookings झाल्या?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: एक 1, दोन 2, तीन 3, चार 4, पाच 5, सहा 6, सात 7, आठ 8, नऊ 9, दहा 10, बारा 12, पंधरा 15, वीस 20, पंचवीस 25, तीस 30, पस्तीस 35, चाळीस 40, पन्नास 50, साठ 60, सत्तर 70, ऐंशी 80, नव्वद 90, शंभर 100, दीडशे 150. Fractions: अर्धा 0.5, दीड 1.5, अडीच 2.5, सव्वा N = N + 0.25, साडे N = N + 0.5, पावणे N = N − 0.25. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Marathi, "वीस-पंचवीस दिवस" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (एकही नाही, एकही झाली नाही, शून्य). dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "आत्ताच्या विक्रीच्या हिशोबाने, आत्ताचा stock किती दिवस पुरेल?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (आठवडा) = 7 days, a month (महिना) = 30 days; so दोन आठवडे 14, तीन आठवडे 21, एक महिना 30, दीड महिना 45, दोन महिने 60, अडीच महिने 75. dispositions.name: discount_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say the discounts and offers they give customers (company schemes count as offers) are, compared with last week, going up, about the same, or coming down? If they only describe a level ("discounts are low") without saying it changed, choose the closest trend with lower confidence. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Marathi or English. The dealer's words may be written in Devanagari (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (माहीत नाही, कल्पना नाही, finance वाल्यांना माहीत). declined when they won't say (सांगणार नाही, सांगता येणार नाही, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said discounts and offers went up (for example जास्त, वाढल्या, वाढतायत, जास्त आल्या, jaast).

The dealer said discounts and offers stayed about the same (for example तेवढ्याच, तितकेच, सारखेच, same, बदल नाही, tevdhech). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said discounts and offers went down (for example कमी, कमी झाल्या, घटल्या, मंदी, kami). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: loan_rejections
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say their customers' vehicle loan rejections, compared with last month, are happening more, about the same, or less? More than last month is high, the same is normal, less is low. If they describe a level instead of a change ("lots of rejections" = high, "normal" = normal), use that. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. objective_options.condition: Rejections are happening more than last month, or are high (for example जास्त होतायत, वाढलेत, bank कडक).
Rejections are about the same as last month, or normal (for example तेवढेच, normal, नॉर्मल, सारखेच).
Rejections are happening less than last month, or are low (for example कमी, कमी झालेत, सहज approve होतात).
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (पुन्हा call करू नका). Just declining this time (नको, interest नाही) is refused. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ठीक आहे, हो, हम्म, बरं), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Marathi or English. The dealer's words may be written in Devanagari (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.
Declined to take part, or didn't want the call recorded (for example नको, interest नाही), without asking for a callback or to stop calls.
Asked to be called back at another time, or said the owner or manager isn't available, before the survey started (for example नंतर call करा, आत्ता busy आहे, संध्याकाळी करा).
Asked not to be called again (for example पुन्हा call करू नका).
Not a vehicle dealership, or the wrong business or person entirely (for example चुकीचा नंबर, हे showroom नाही).

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
